slides.title: Not one lock, but layers
slides.text: The post office never trusts a single lock. A strong door guards the hall, a safe guards the packages, and only Pim's key opens the safe. Three layers, one job.
slides.alt: Lock 6, Layers: a snooper tries to peek inside a sealed note. Four layers wait: padlock, key checker, patch crew, copy vault.

focus.cue: One trouble card: a snooper peeks
Four layers, each stops a different trick

slides.title: Updates patch holes
slides.text: When a game or tablet asks to update, it is patching holes. A hole is a small flaw a trickster could climb through, and the update sews it shut.
slides.alt: Threat 3 of 4: an old lock has a known hole that anyone can use. The Patch Crew waits among the layers.

focus.cue: An old lock has a known hole
Updates, the Patch Crew, sew it shut

slides.title: Backups beat accidents
slides.text: A backup is a spare copy of your things, kept somewhere else. If a tablet breaks or gets locked by a trick, a safe copy elsewhere means nothing precious is lost.
slides.alt: Threat 4 of 4: a flood soaks the only copy of a letter. The Copy Vault keeps a spare somewhere else.

focus.cue: A flood soaks the only copy
A spare kept somewhere else saves it

slides.title: Build your layer stack
slides.text: Pim is checking a home tablet before Spark Day. Check each layer that should be guarding it.
steps: A lock screen that asks for a key
A passphrase only its owner knows
A backup copy kept somewhere else

slides.title: Two weak layers can win
slides.text: No single layer is perfect, and that is fine. Two ordinary layers together can beat one strong one, because a trick that slips past the first still meets the second.
slides.alt: Threat 2 of 4: a guesser tries key after key on a mailbox. Which layer stops it?

focus.cue: A guesser tries key after key
A second layer, the key checker, still stands

one guard in a stack of guards
to fix a hole so it cannot be used
to keep people and things safe from harm
